seo.description: Tree and shrub pruning, removals, invasive plant control and clearing in Greater Victoria, with permit checks under local tree bylaws. Get a free quote.

hero.h1: Tree pruning, removal and vegetation management
hero.lede: Pruning, removals, invasive plant control and brush clearing, with a check of your municipality's tree bylaw before any cut.

localContext: Most Greater Victoria municipalities protect native trees such as Garry oak and arbutus, and the rules on size, pruning and permits differ from one to the next.
goodFitIf: Branches hang over your roof, driveway or the sidewalk.
A hedge has grown too tall or wide and needs to come back in stages.
English ivy, Himalayan blackberry or Scotch broom is taking over a yard, lot or trail edge.
You need to know whether a tree is protected before anyone cuts it.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remove a tree?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Most municipalities in Greater Victoria have a tree bylaw, and many protect native species such as Garry oak and arbutus at small sizes. The rules differ, so we check yours before any work. See our [area pages](/areas/) for local links.

faqs.q: Will you apply for the permit?
faqs.a: We can help you prepare the information the municipality asks for. The permit decision is the municipality's.
No. Topping harms trees, and bylaws in the region restrict it; North Saanich's tree bylaw prohibits it. See our [North Saanich page](/areas/north-saanich/).
Our current certifications are listed here: [CERTIFICATIONS].

faqs.q: Can you prune or clear during nesting season?
faqs.a: Sometimes. B.C.'s Wildlife Act protects a bird's nest while it holds birds or eggs, so in spring and summer we check for nests before cutting and plan the work around any we find.

faqs.q: What happens to the invasive plants you remove?
faqs.a: We keep them apart from other green waste and take them to a disposal site that accepts them, following CRD guidance. Knotweed needs special handling and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.
